messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The test `testInfiniteLoop` is designed to check the behavior of HelpFormatter when wrapping long option descriptions inside a narrow width (20 characters). The issue reported is that HelpFormatter enters an infinite loop when a word is too long to fit on a single line.

From the source code:
- `HelpFormatter.printHelp(String, Options)` calls `printHelp(int, String, String, Options, String, boolean)` with the default width.
- The latter calls `printHelp(PrintWriter, int, String, String, Options, int, int, String, boolean)` which eventually calls `printOptions(PrintWriter, int, Options, int, int)`.
- `printOptions` calls `renderOptions(StringBuffer, int, Options, int, int)`.
- `renderOptions` iterates over options and calls `renderWrappedText(StringBuffer, int, int, String)` with the option text (including description).
- The method `renderWrappedText` attempts to wrap the provided text based on width. It looks for a wrapping position using `findWrapPos`.
- If no wrap position is found (`pos == -1`), it appends the trimmed text as is and returns.
- Otherwise, it appends the wrapped substring and continues to wrap the rest in a loop.
- In the loop, the code guards against an infinite loop by checking if the current wrap position equals the previous wrap position (`pos == lastPos`). If so, it throws a `RuntimeException` to avoid the infinite loop (with message CLI-162).

The reported infinite loop happens because the original code did not have this exception and would continue looping forever.

The test reproduces the infinite loop by setting the width to 20 and supplying an option description with a very long word (looooong), which cannot be wrapped by spaces since the word itself is longer than the width.

Thus, `findWrapPos` presumably returns a position that does not advance on each iteration, causing the loop on line 822 to never terminate.

However, from the code we see that this has been fixed by detecting when no progress happens in the wrapper and throwing a RuntimeException with a message.

Hence, the test comment "used to hang & crash" is consistent with the previous behavior; the current code mitigates infinite looping by throwing an exception.

In conclusion, the infinite loop was caused because the wrapping logic in `renderWrappedText` did not properly handle cases where no wrapping position advances, e.g., when a single word is longer than the line width, causing an infinite loop. The fix implemented is to detect this scenario and throw an exception to avoid hanging.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this issue. The problem and fix are localized to the wrapping logic in `HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText`.

This explains the failure: the test triggered what used to be an infinite loop, but with the current fix, the exception is thrown.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
